meta.scope: Active single-image ads from the Facebook Ad Library (CA), sorted by total impressions. Rank = position among the 189 captured single-image ads in that sort (1 = highest impressions). Videos/carousels excluded. The page reports ~430 active ads overall.
takeaways: Repo cars are the workhorse angle: 48 of 189 ads (15 unique creatives), including 5 of the top 10 and 23 of the top 50 by impressions. Counting rentals, demos and ex-fleet too, the "cheaper source than a regular car" family is 74 ads.

The #1 ad by impressions is a seller ad ("Don't Sell Your Car Privately / Do this instead…"). The sell-my-car funnel is 36 ads across 3 stages: skip the private sale, your car is worth more, and book your inspection before your quote expires.

Bad or any credit is the near-universal offer: it appears on 47 of 97 unique creatives, plus $0 down (18) and pre-approval in minutes (21). 145 of 189 ads click through to the apply.canadadrives.ca pre-approval form, 16 of them to /powersports.

Their newest big bet is payment-led proof: "Cheap financing from $170 bi-weekly" / "Real Payments. Real Approvals." 20 ads launched Oct 14, 2026 from 5 creatives with 10 versions each, so 27 ads total. None rank in the top 50 yet.

"Don't buy X… buy Y instead" is the signature pattern interrupt, used across repo, rental, demo, fleet and seller ads (15 creatives). The same hooks get reshot in many formats: handheld signs, words in snow or frost, tweet or Reddit posts, cartoons, gradient text.

The creative style is low-fi and native rather than branded: lot-banner photos (21 creatives), handheld signs (15), words written on cars (10), UGC-style tweet or Reddit posts (7). Only about 18 use bold promo graphics.

Seasonal and geo: 26 creatives use winter or snow imagery, including a "buy in fall/winter" pro-tip. Powersports (cheap snowmobiles and ATVs) is a fresh test of 17 one-off creatives launched Sep 24 – Oct 16. Geo-targeting is rare: only one Alberta ad and one newcomers-to-Canada ad.

texts:
Looking for a great deal on a used vehicle? 

Consider buying a used demo vehicle. A demo vehicle is a car that has been used by the dealership or manufacturer for display purposes, test drives, or as a loaner vehicle for service customers. Here are some reasons why someone might consider purchasing a used demo vehicle:

Lower price: Demo vehicles are typically sold at a discounted price compared to brand new cars. Even though they might have some mileage on them, the savings can be significant, making them more affordable for budget-conscious buyers.

Relatively new and well-maintained: Demo vehicles are usually late-model cars that have been on the road for a relatively short time. They are often well-maintained and kept in excellent condition since the dealership uses them to showcase their products.

meta.scope: Active video ads from the Facebook Ad Library (CA), sorted by total impressions. Rank = position among the 99 captured video ads in that sort (1 = highest impressions); it is a separate ranking from the image ads. Transcripts are automatic (Whisper) and may contain small errors.
takeaways: One cheap template owns the top of the video ranking: a 19-second voiceover ("If you're looking for a cheap car in <city>, now is the perfect time to buy… massive year-end inventory clearance deals… before someone else gets the car you want") over the same Bronco, dealer-lot and phone b-roll. It is re-voiced for 11 towns (13 cuts, 16 ads) and holds 7 of the top 10. 7 of the 13 cuts run with repo-car copy, so the video sells timing while the caption sells repos.

Repo cars still take #1: a 10-second clip with no voiceover, "Don't buy a new car in Calgary… buy a used repo instead", handwritten on a car's rear hatch. It was reshot for Grande Prairie, Kamloops and Golden. Repo is 9 videos and 15 ads, 12 of them in the top 50.

Long-form creator videos work: 6 talking-head videos of 80–88 s (14 ads) rank #7, #9, #11, #17, #25 and #48. The same bearded creator in a pink jacket films from his driver's seat, often replying to a TikTok-style comment ("I only make $30k/year… buying a car is impossible", "When is the best time to buy a car in Canada?").

Credit is the biggest video angle by ads (9 videos, 21 ads). It is framed as "get pre-approved first so you're never turned down at the last step" ("Your credit is just a number, not a verdict"). Pre-approval in minutes appears in 41 of 58 videos, and 84 of 99 video ads click through to apply.canadadrives.ca.

Video is where local targeting lives: 22 towns are named in voiceovers, copy or link captions ("Cheap Cars in Kingston"), concentrated in Alberta (11 videos), then Saskatchewan, BC, Ontario and Nova Scotia. The image set had a single Alberta ad.

The newest bets are ex-demo cars and seller ads. Demo is 8 UGC videos and 17 ads, all launched Sep 22 – Oct 16 ("Nobody really talks about this…", "I thought this was a scam at first"), but the best rank is only #39. On Oct 20, new seller ads launched: "We want to buy your car!" sticky notes on a steering wheel under the headline "Selling Your Car Privately Is Dead", plus fresh copies of the fake-TV-news and walk-and-talk seller videos.

Production is native and lo-fi: 47 of 58 videos have voiceover with burned-in captions, and the median length is 18.6 s (12 are ≤10 s). About 25 are creator-led (talking head, PiP over car b-roll, walk-and-talk). Only 4 are motion graphics and 3 are fake TV-news segments. There is no polished brand spot.
meta.mix_note: Videos lean harder than images on clearance/timing (18% of video ads vs 7% of image ads), demo cars (17% vs 3%) and credit/pre-approval (21% vs 11%). Images lean on repo cars (25% vs 15%), real-payment proof (14% vs 2%), powersports (9% vs 1%) and ex-fleet (5% vs 0%). Seller ads are 13% of both. "Car shopping made easy" (testimonials, review cards, a friend's referral) appears only on video. [live-update test]

Lower price: Demo vehicles are typically sold at a discounted price compared to brand new cars. Even though they might have some mileage on them, the savings can be significant, making them more affordable for budget-conscious buyers.

Relatively new and well-maintained: Demo vehicles are usually late-model cars that have been on the road for a relatively short time. They are often well-maintained and kept in excellent condition since the dealership uses them to showcase their products.

Fewer previous owners: Unlike traditional used cars that may have had multiple owners, demo vehicles generally have only been driven by dealership staff or potential customers on test drives.

Manufacturer's warranty: Most demo vehicles are still covered under the original manufacturer's warranty, providing added peace of mind to the buyer.

Upgraded features: Demo vehicles often come with additional features and options that were used to showcase the car's full potential. As a result, buyers may get access to premium features at a lower price compared to custom-ordering a new vehicle.

Immediate availability: Unlike new cars that might require waiting for production and delivery, demo vehicles are readily available at the dealership, allowing buyers to drive away sooner.

Demo vehicles come in a wide range of makes, models, and years. Whether you're in the market for a compact car, a spacious SUV, or a sporty sedan, we can help you find the perfect car and get a great deal.
